issuing_body: Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC), National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC), Ministry of Education (MOE), Ministry of Science and Technology (MOST), Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT), Ministry of Public Security (MPS), and National Radio and Television Administration (NRTA)
covered_actors: Generative AI service providers offering services to the public within the People's Republic of China (including via programmable interfaces/APIs)
Offshore generative AI service providers offering services into the People's Republic of China
prohibited_practices: Generating content prohibited by laws and administrative regulations, including content that incites subversion of state power or overthrow of the socialist system, endangers national security and interests, damages national image, incites separatism or undermines national unity and social stability, promotes terrorism, extremism, ethnic hatred or discrimination, violence, obscenity/pornography, or false and harmful information
Using advantages in algorithms, data, or platforms to implement monopolies and unfair competition
Endangering others' physical or mental health, or infringing others' portrait rights, reputation rights, honor rights, privacy rights, and personal information rights
Infringing others' lawful intellectual property rights during training data processing

Collecting unnecessary personal information, illegally retaining user input information and usage records capable of identifying users, or illegally providing user input information and usage records to others
enforcement_authorities: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT)
compliance_deadlines: 2023-08-15: Effective date of the Interim Measures (Article 24)
penalties_summary: Violations are punished by competent authorities under the Cybersecurity Law, Data Security Law, Personal Information Protection Law, and Science and Technology Progress Law. Where not otherwise specified by law or administrative regulation, competent authorities issue warnings, circulated criticisms, and orders for rectification within a time limit; refusal to rectify or serious circumstances result in orders to suspend provision of relevant services. Public security violations incur public security administrative penalties, and criminal offenses incur criminal liability. For non-compliant offshore services offered into China, the national cyberspace authority notifies relevant agencies to take technical and other necessary disposal measures.
implementation_notes: Applies to generative AI services (generating text, images, audio, video, etc.) provided to the public in China, while exempting organizations, enterprises, educational/research institutions, and public cultural or professional institutions that develop and apply generative AI without serving the domestic public (Art. 2). Establishes an inclusive, prudent, and classified/graded regulatory approach (Art. 3, Art. 16). Links compliance to existing regimes: content labeling under the Deep Synthesis Provisions (Art. 12), security assessment and algorithm filing for services with public opinion attributes or social mobilization capabilities under the Algorithm Recommendation Provisions (Art. 17), and applicable administrative licensing and foreign investment laws (Art. 23).
